questions.question: Farad (F) is the SI unit of which physical quantity?
questions.explanation: Capacitance C = Q/V is measured in Farads (F), where 1 Farad = 1 Coulomb per Volt.

questions.question: The total charge of how many electrons equals 100 µC?
Which of the following pairs of charges will produce the greatest attractive electrostatic force at a fixed distance r?
questions.explanation: Attractive force requires opposite charges. Between -q & +4q, |q₁q₂| = 4q². Between -2q & +2q, |q₁q₂| = 4q². Opposite signs make both attractive with magnitude 4kq²/r².

questions.question: In a series combination of capacitors, which quantity remains the same across each capacitor?
questions.explanation: In series, current flows equally into each plate, so every capacitor stores identical charge Q (Q₁ = Q₂ = Q₃ = Q).

questions.question: Four identical 1 µF capacitors are connected electrically. What is the least possible equivalent capacitance?
questions.explanation: Least capacitance is obtained in series: 1/Ceq = 1/1 + 1/1 + 1/1 + 1/1 = 4, so Ceq = 1/4 µF = 0.25 µF.

questions.question: If the charge on the plates of a fixed capacitor is doubled, the potential difference across its plates will:
questions.explanation: From V = Q/C, for constant capacitance C, potential difference V is directly proportional to charge Q.

questions.question: The value of Coulomb's constant k = 1 / (4πε) depends primarily on:

options.B: Medium between charges and system of units

questions.explanation: Coulomb's constant k depends on the permittivity of the surrounding medium (ε) and the choice of units (in SI vacuum, k ≈ 9 × 10⁹ N m²/C²).

questions.question: If a test charge of 4 µC is placed in a uniform electric field of strength 2 N/C, what force will it experience?
The SI unit of electric potential (Volt) is equivalent to:
questions.explanation: Electric potential V = W/q (work done per unit charge), so 1 Volt = 1 Joule per Coulomb (J C⁻¹).

questions.question: Two charges are initially 4 cm apart. When moved closer to 1 cm apart, the electrostatic force between them becomes:
questions.explanation: Coulomb's force F ∝ 1/r². Since distance decreases by a factor of 4 (from 4 cm to 1 cm), force increases by 4² = 16 times.
